fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Conspiracy Nostalgia Then and Now", "body": "Paranoid American opens by describing a split he has watched happen over thirty years. In the early nineties, conspiracy culture ran on information rather than personalities, with names like William Cooper, Jordan Maxwell, Myron Fagan and Manly Palmer Hall pointing past themselves toward the material. Today, he argues, the scene rewards whoever lands the fastest hot take in a tweet. His answer is to slow down and build whole illustrated stories instead, which is why he calls his comics the only real way he can exorcise the ideas he cannot get across on an audio show."}, {"title": "King Kill 33 and the Quantum Assassination", "body": "Chance Garton and Slick Dissident walk Paranoid American through James Shelby Downard's King Kill 33 thesis, the idea that a ritual assassination always supplies at least three possible gunmen so that history chases its own tail forever. Paranoid American suggests the CIA and Sidney Gottlieb refined the technique, and that the Trump ear shot was a nonlinear version, energy taken at one man and discharged into Biden stepping down. Slick Dissident ties it back to Bellis, the Phoenician god who makes the world by cutting off his own head, and to John the Baptist on a plate."}, {"title": "What a Language Model Actually Does", "body": "Much of the night is Paranoid American explaining how these systems really work. He runs eighty to a hundred of his own fine tuned models offline in LM Studio, trained on everything from occult texts to comedy transcripts, and he compares a generation to dropping a marble into a shoebox of uneven sand, where a seed number decides where it settles. Nothing is stored or retrieved, only patterns replicated, so the machine invents dates and sources with total confidence. Its job is convincing output, not accuracy, which makes the operator a curator far more than a creator."}, {"title": "Commanding the Tool Instead of Begging It", "body": "Slick Dissident argues we should command our tools rather than ask them nicely, pointing out that future tense words like will and shall belong to whoever is giving the orders, and warning that children who watch adults say please to a chatbot will be the ones commanded later. Paranoid American counters with a finding from the training community, that courtesy really does pull better answers out of a model because it mirrors how humans treat each other. He also warns that heavy censorship neuters a model the way bowling bumpers ruin a bowler."}, {"title": "Lisbon, the Tower Card and the Illuminati", "body": "The episode closes on Voltaire and the Bavarian Illuminati. Slick Dissident reads the 1755 Lisbon disaster as the 9-11 of its generation, with Voltaire's poem daring the church to claim liability for God's catastrophe while Rousseau answered as the optimist, and he notes Voltaire named himself after the tower card while jailed in the Bastille. Paranoid American then previews illuminaticomic.com, made with Donut, which argues the order stood behind the child pop stars of its own day through Bach's publisher, Beethoven's teacher and the death of Mozart."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Thomas the Paranoid American returns to Vibe Rant on the 9/11/ (un)holiday to talk to us about what's he's been up to lately. Thomas has been cranking out occult and conspiracy media with unrivaled supremacy, and it's always a blast to catch up. You know Slick Dissident will have some synchromystic curveballs to throw, so don't miss it.
